rationale: Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-014 (illustrative figures), A-1: without the quota Calvar would keep importing well over 350,000 tonnes a year (about 750,000 now), so the quota binds from the first year.

Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-014 (illustrative figures), A-2: customs enforces the quota at the ports; only two ports admit bulk cargo, every shipment is inspected, and imports without rights are seized and fined three times their value.

Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-014 (illustrative figures), A-12: bulk sugar is smuggled on a meaningful scale; bulk entry is port-only with inspection, so evasion is below the cut-off.
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-014 (illustrative figures), A-21: growers, quota holders and manufacturers can organize at a cost below their stake.
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-014 (illustrative figures), A-5: holders, growers and landowners expect the quota to survive the five-year review.
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-014 (illustrative figures), A-3: domestic beet sugar and refined imported sugar are close substitutes for buyers.
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-014 (illustrative figures), A-17: lower imports are not offset by capital flows or other adjustments within the medium horizon.
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-014 (illustrative figures), A-22: the customs budget is raised to cover inspection of bulk shipments and the register of quota rights.
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-014 (illustrative figures), A-6: importers know the allocation formula during the window and can finance and store extra imports.
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-014 (illustrative figures), A-8: importing blends and syrups with 65% sugar or less is technically and commercially workable for some users.
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-014 (illustrative figures), A-21: growers, quota holders and manufacturers can organize at a cost below their stake.
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-014 (illustrative figures), A-5: holders, growers and landowners expect the quota to survive the five-year review.
No matching assumption in WE-014; judged from the text: the holders range from two port refineries to smaller traders, whose costs and uses of the right differ.
No matching assumption in WE-014; judged from the text: shares are permanent, may be sold or leased, and transfers are registered with customs.
